dimensions.summary: Graph owns a domain conformance boundary over four public Shared subpaths; contract identity moved to the Graph contracts layer and neither package imports the central CLI.
The registry-derived gate requires exactly one adoption record for every registered Shared-dependent package, while unregistered placeholder consumers remain forbidden.
The adoption boundary reuses bounded Shared validation and registry lookup; the complete Graph tarball remains 6,737 of 262,144 compressed bytes.
The boundary fails closed for malformed or unsupported Core envelopes, foreign producers, unsupported Graph schemas, cancellation and implicit domain migration.
Rejected adoption results contain bounded diagnostics without returning or echoing the untrusted domain payload, and the boundary performs no filesystem, network or telemetry operation.
Platform-neutral ESM, local Linux execution and isolated tarball installation pass; macOS and Windows remote evidence remains pending.
Shared remains a zero-runtime-dependency leaf; Graph depends only on the exact development Shared version; publication and the CLI bridge remain prohibited.
Graph's 20 tests and Shared's 107 tests pass; exact current artifacts deterministically produce an accepted result with the generated registry contract digest.
Shared Core negotiation remains reusable, but a migrated envelope returns domain-contract-migration-required instead of silently authorizing a Graph payload version.
Every rejection has a typed stable status and bounded diagnostic; Shared cancellation propagates without partial domain interpretation.
One machine adoption manifest, one executable registry/DAG guard and canonical documentation keep implementation, public claims and stage state aligned.
Separately packed Shared and Graph tarballs install with lifecycle scripts disabled; the installed Graph consumer executes the adoption boundary while development paths remain excluded.
